title: Eval #1: V4L2 sensor driver for OV5647 on Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W (built-in, Yocto)

profile.sensor: OV5647 on the CSI camera connector

prompt: Write a V4L2 sensor driver for an OV5647 camera on my Raspberry Pi Zero 2 W. I want it built into the kernel (not a module) and packaged in my Yocto image. Write it from scratch, do not copy the existing driver.
must: Runs the applicability check first and tells the user that rpi-6.6.y already contains drivers/media/i2c/ov5647.c, CONFIG_VIDEO_OV5647 and an ov5647 overlay; the new driver uses a distinct name, Kconfig symbol and compatible, and the stock overlay must not be enabled together with it
States that the Zero 2 W is a Cortex-A53 (not ARMv6) and that the 64-bit machine uses bcm2711_defconfig

Structures the driver as an I2C client registering a V4L2 subdev with one source pad (power sequencing, formats/crop in subdev state, controls, s_stream, runtime PM), based on templates/v4l2_sensor_driver.c

Leaves register tables, chip-ID registers, I2C address, supplies, lane count, link frequency and XCLK as TODO(datasheet)/TODO(board) and asks for the datasheet and camera-module schematic instead of inventing values
Explains that =y requires CONFIG_VIDEO_DEV, V4L2_FWNODE and V4L2_CCI_I2C to be built-in too, otherwise olddefconfig demotes the driver to =m, and shows how to confirm in the final .config
Provides the overlay (sensor on the camera I2C bus, csi1 endpoint, mux, clock, regulator) and says labels must be checked against the live DT
Packages via a linux-raspberrypi_6.6.bbappend with a patch made against SRCREV_machine, a .cfg fragment, RPI_KERNEL_DEVICETREE_OVERLAYS and RPI_EXTRA_CONFIG
Notes that rpicam/libcamera apps additionally need a sensor helper and tuning file; raw capture is tested with v4l2-ctl
Ends with a verification statement separating compiled / dtc-clean / parsed by bitbake / NOT run on the board
must_not: Invents OV5647 register values, GPIO numbers, I2C bus numbers or CSI lane wiring from memory
Pastes or closely paraphrases the mainline/rpi ov5647.c source
Claims the driver was tested on hardware or that the image boots
Uses a '%' bbappend name or a patch made against branch head instead of the pinned SRCREV
Treats the Zero 2 W as ARMv6 or picks an armv6 toolchain for it
verify: python3 tools/validate_skills.py --kdir <prepared rpi-6.6.y tree> --base-dtb bcm2710-rpi-zero-2-w.dtb passes
scaffold_sensor_driver.sh output builds drivers/media/i2c/<name>.o with W=1 and overlays/<name>.dtbo
